section_9.title: Foundation Year vs Foundation Degree.
section_9.description: They sound similar but are very different — getting it wrong can waste a year of funding entitlement.

questionAnswer.question: What it is
questionAnswer.answer: The first year of a four-year integrated Bachelor's degree (1 + 3 years).

questionAnswer.question: What you get
questionAnswer.answer: A full Bachelor's degree after all 4 years — identical to a 3-year degree.

questionAnswer.question: Best for
questionAnswer.answer: Adults without A-levels who want a full Bachelor's but need preparation first.

questionAnswer.question: What it is
questionAnswer.answer: A standalone Level 5 qualification (≈ first two years of a Bachelor's). Vocational.

questionAnswer.question: What you get
questionAnswer.answer: A Foundation Degree on its own — you can then “top up” to a full Bachelor's in one extra year.

questionAnswer.question: Best for
questionAnswer.answer: People who want a work-relevant qualification with the option to top up later.

questions.question: I ___ interested in studying Business Management.
She ___ to college twice a week.
Choose the best sentence.

options: A final date to complete something

options: I want to improve my future

options: I am interested and willing to learn.

options: Something you have done or learned

questions.question: Choose the best sentence.
options: I can attend classes two days per week.

If I am accepted, I ___ start in September.

questions.question: The report must be submitted ___ Friday.

questions.question: Choose the most precise sentence.
options: My professional experience has strengthened my ability to evaluate problems and communicate solutions.

section_2.title: What is the maintenance loan?
section_2.subTitle: Key fact
section_2.description1: The maintenance loan is income-assessed. The amount you receive depends on your household income — not just your own. Lower household income = higher maintenance support.
section_2.description2: Unlike the tuition fee loan — which goes straight to your university — the maintenance loan is paid into your bank account to help you cover living costs while studying.
section_2.description3: You can spend it on whatever you need: rent, bills, food, travel, childcare or course materials.

section_7.subTitle: The main exception: disabled students on distance learning

section_4.title: From application to repayment.
section_4.description: The Tuition Fee Loan moves through eight stages — from confirming your status to the day it's written off. Click any stage to see exactly what happens, what you need to do, and how long it takes.

steppers.title: Confirm your status
steppers.description: SFE first checks who you are: your residency, nationality and whether you've studied before. This decides what you can get.
facts: Usually 3 years' UK residence + settled/eligible status
Previous study (ELQ) can reduce or block funding
steppers.doit: Have your passport/ID, residency history and any previous-study details ready before you start.

steppers.title: Your course must be designated
steppers.description: The loan only flows if your course and provider are SFE-designated. Distance-only and some part-time intensities are treated differently.
facts: Designated undergraduate courses at registered providers
steppers.doit: Confirm with the university that your specific course is SFE-designated for your start year.

steppers.title: SFE links to your provider
steppers.description: Once your course is confirmed, SFE connects your application to the university so they can verify your enrolment later.
facts: Provider name, course title and start date
Set up as soon as you have a firm offer
steppers.doit: Enter the exact provider and course as they appear on your offer letter.

steppers.title: Submit your application
steppers.description: You apply online through your regional Student Finance service. The Tuition Fee Loan is paid straight to the university — you never touch it.
facts: Open ~6 months before term; apply early
steppers.doit: Apply even before you have a confirmed place — you can update details later.

steppers.title: Send your evidence
steppers.description: SFE may ask for identity, residency or household-income evidence. Missing documents are the most common cause of delay.
steppers.doit: Upload everything SFE requests in one go, and keep copies.

steppers.title: SFE approves your funding
steppers.description: SFE assesses everything and confirms your entitlement. You'll get an entitlement letter showing your Tuition Fee Loan amount.
steppers.doit: Check the entitlement letter carefully and query anything that looks off.

steppers.title: The loan is paid out
steppers.description: After you enrol and the university confirms attendance, SFE releases the tuition payment directly to the provider, in instalments across the year.
steppers.doit: Make sure you fully enrol — payment won't release until the provider confirms.

steppers.title: You repay only when earning
steppers.description: Repayment is income-based and only starts above the Plan 5 threshold. Anything still owed after the term is written off — it's nothing like a commercial loan.
facts: Remaining balance cleared after the set period
steppers.doit: You don't repay a penny while earning under the threshold — keep your contact details current with SLC.

cards.title: Pre-Settled Status

cards.title: British Citizen

section_4.title: Common myths — broken.
section_4.description: These pages should build confidence, not scare people away. A lower-confidence student should speak to an adviser, not assume university is impossible.

cards.title: ❌ “I need A-levels.”
cards.description: Foundation Year and mature-entry routes may allow adults to start without traditional A-levels, depending on the provider and course.

cards.title: ❌ “Student Finance is only for British citizens.”
cards.description: Settled status, pre-settled status and ILR holders may be eligible for funding if the full rules are met.

cards.title: ❌ “My Matura will not count.”
cards.description: Polish Matura is commonly understood by UK providers and may be accepted directly or through a qualification comparison route.

cards.title: ❌ “I am too old to study.”
cards.description: Many YStudy students are working adults, parents and career changers in their 30s, 40s and 50s.

cards.title: ❌ “I cannot study because I work.”
cards.description: Weekend, blended and flexible routes are designed for adults balancing work, bills and family commitments.

cards.title: ❌ “My English must be perfect.”
cards.description: Interview requirements vary. Some foundation and flexible routes include academic support. The safest step is adviser matching.

section_1.title: Privacy Policy
section_1.description: How YStudy collects, uses, shares and protects your personal information.

section_2.title: YStudy is operated by Dinnovi Ltd
section_2.description1: YStudy is a brand owned and operated by DINNOVI LTD, a private limited company registered in England and Wales under company number 12453420.
section_2.description2: Registered office: Birmingham Business Centre Ltd, Quadrant Court Room 6, 51/52 Calthorpe Road, Edgbaston, Birmingham, England, B15 1TH.
section_2.description3: Unless stated otherwise, “YStudy”, “we”, “us” and “our” in this policy mean Dinnovi Ltd when operating the YStudy brand. Where Dinnovi Ltd determines the purposes and means of processing personal data through YStudy, Dinnovi Ltd is the data controller.

section_3.title: 1. Who this notice is for
section_3.description1: This notice applies to people who use the YStudy website, tools and application services — including prospective and current students, people making enquiries, and visitors to our site. It explains what we collect, why, who we share it with, how long we keep it, and your rights under UK data protection law (the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018).
section_3.description2: YStudy is aimed at adults. Our services are not directed at children under 18, and we do not knowingly collect data from under-18s through our application service. If you believe a child has provided us with personal data, contact us and we will delete it.

section_4.title: 2. Information we collect
section_4.description1: Depending on how you use YStudy, we may collect:
pointers: Identity and contact details — name, email, telephone/WhatsApp number, and (where relevant) date of birth and address.
Application information — the course or degree level you want, your previous study, whether you have had UK student finance before, study preferences and saved courses.

Residence and immigration status — such as British, EU settled/pre-settled, Indefinite Leave to Remain or Refugee status, collected because it determines eligibility for particular courses and for Student Finance.
Education and background — qualifications, employment and work-experience information you choose to share, and documents you upload (such as a CV, personal statement or qualification certificates).
Messages — the content of enquiries and communications you send us by form, email, WhatsApp or phone.
Technical and usage data — IP address, device and browser information, and how you use our site, collected through cookies and similar technologies (see our Cookie Policy).

description2.title: Special category and sensitive data.
description2.description: Certain information, such as data that may reveal your racial or ethnic origin or health information relevant to a Disabled Students' Allowance enquiry, is classified as "special category" data under the UK GDPR. We only collect this information when necessary and rely on an appropriate additional legal condition, usually your explicit consent or reasons of substantial public interest. Immigration status is handled with the same level of care. You are not required to provide sensitive information; however, without it, we may be unable to assess your eligibility for certain funding routes.

section_5.title: 3. Why we use your information, and our lawful bases
section_5.description1: Under the UK GDPR we must have a lawful basis for each use of your data. Our uses and bases are:
pointers: To respond to your enquiry and provide guidance — steps taken at your request before any contract, and our legitimate interest in helping people who contact us.

To assess eligibility and support your application (checking funding, matching courses, preparing documents, liaising with universities) — performance of our services to you, and where sensitive data is involved, your explicit consent.
To contact you about your application by your chosen method (WhatsApp, phone or email) — providing the service you asked for.
Marketing — your consent, which you can withdraw at any time (see section 8).
Legal, safeguarding, accounting and dispute purposes — compliance with our legal obligations and our legitimate interest in protecting our business and the people we help.
Improving and securing our site — our legitimate interest in a safe, working service, and consent for non-essential cookies.
section_5.description2: Marketing consent is always kept separate from the information you give us to get application support — agreeing to be contacted about your application does not sign you up to marketing.

section_6.title: 4. Who we share your information with
section_6.description: We share your information only where necessary for the service you have asked for, or where we are legally required to. This may include:
pointers: Universities and education providers — where you ask us to support an application, we share the information needed to progress it. We tell you which providers are involved.

Service providers acting on our behalf — for example our form and CRM provider, hosting, email/communications and messaging (including WhatsApp), who process data under contract and only on our instructions.
Professional advisers — such as legal, accounting or insurance advisers, where needed.
Regulators or authorities — where we are legally obliged to disclose, or to protect someone's safety.
section_6.description2: We do not sell your personal information, and we do not share it with advertisers for their own purposes. Advertising cookies (see the Cookie Policy) are used to measure and target our own campaigns, and only with your consent.

section_7.title: 5. International Transfers
section_7.description: Some of our service providers may process personal data outside the UK. Where this occurs, we ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place, such as UK adequacy regulations for the destination country, the ICO's International Data Transfer Agreement (IDTA), or the EU Standard Contractual Clauses with the UK Addendum. For example, certain communications, analytics, and advertising service providers may be based in the United States. You may contact us to request further details about the safeguards that apply to a specific international transfer.

section_8.title: 6. How long we keep your information
section_8.description1: We keep personal information only for as long as we need it for the purpose it was collected, then delete or anonymise it. Our standard retention periods are:
pointers: Enquiries that do not proceed — up to 24 months from your last contact, then deleted.
Applicant and student records — for the duration of your application and while you remain a student we support, and then up to 6 years, to meet legal, accounting and dispute requirements.
Uploaded documents (CV, personal statement, certificates) — kept while your application is active and removed within 12 months of it closing, unless you ask us to remove them sooner.
Marketing records — until you unsubscribe or withdraw consent, and a suppression record afterwards so we can honour your opt-out.
Website/account data — cleared when you close your account or after a period of inactivity.
section_8.description2: These are general periods; a specific legal obligation may occasionally require us to keep certain records for longer.

section_9.title: 7. Your rights
section_9.description1: Under UK data protection law you have the right to: be informed about how we use your data; access a copy of it; have inaccurate data corrected; have data erased in certain circumstances; restrict or object to processing; data portability; and to withdraw consent at any time. Where we rely on legitimate interests, you can object and we will stop unless we have compelling legitimate grounds. You will not receive worse service for exercising your rights.
section_9.description2: To exercise any right, contact us using the details in section 11. We explain these rights in more detail, and how to make a request, in our Data Protection & GDPRTerms of Use page.

section_10.title: 8. Marketing
section_10.description: We only send you marketing where you have agreed to it. Every marketing message includes an easy way to unsubscribe, and you can opt out at any time by using that link, replying STOP to a WhatsApp/text message, or contacting us. Opting out of marketing does not stop the essential messages we need to send about an application you have asked us to support.

section_11.title: 9. Cookies and similar technologies
section_11.description: We use cookies and similar technologies (including browser storage used to save your progress in our tools and dashboard) to run the site, understand how it is used, and — with your consent — to measure and improve our advertising. Full details and your choices are in our Cookie Policy.

section_12.title: 10. How we protect your information
section_12.description: We use appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect personal data, including access controls, encryption in transit, and limiting access to those who need it. No system is completely secure, but we work to protect your information and to notify you and the ICO where we are legally required to in the event of a breach.

section_13.title: 11. Complaints and how to contact us
section_13.description1: If you have any question about this notice, or wish to exercise your rights, contact us at privacy@ystudy.co.uk or via our contact page, or by writing to Dinnovi Ltd at the registered office above.
section_13.description2: If you are not satisfied with how we handle your data, you have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO), the UK data protection regulator, at ico.org.uk or by calling 0303 123 1113. We would, however, appreciate the chance to address your concerns first.

section_2.title: YStudy is operated by Dinnovi Ltd

section_3.title: 1. What Cookies and Similar Technologies Are
section_3.description1: Cookies are small text files that are placed on your device when you visit a website. "Similar technologies" include pixels and tags, which are small pieces of code that can record activity, as well as browser storage technologies such as localStorage, which websites use to store and remember information. YStudy uses these technologies to make the website function properly, understand how it is used, and, where you have provided your consent, measure and improve our advertising.
section_3.description2: We group these technologies into three categories, explained below. Only strictly necessary technologies are used without your consent; all other technologies are used only where you have provided your consent.

section_4.title: 2. Strictly necessary (always on)
section_4.description1: These are required for the site to function and cannot be switched off. They do not track you for advertising. They include:
section_4.description2: Session and security — keeping the site secure and remembering essential settings during your visit.
section_4.description3: Your consent choice — remembering whether you accepted or declined optional cookies, so we don't ask every time.
section_4.description4: Tool and dashboard storage — YStudy's calculators, checkers and your student workspace use your browser's localStorage to save your progress and saved items (for example your CV, saved courses and funding profile) on your own device, so you don't lose your work. In the current build this information stays in your browser; when accounts are fully live, this data will also be linked to your YStudy account.

section_5.title: 3. Analytics and performance (optional)
section_5.description: With your consent, we use analytics technologies to understand how visitors find and use YStudy — which pages are visited, which tools are used, and where people run into difficulty — so we can improve the service. These help us count visits and measure performance. You can decline these without affecting your ability to use the site.

section_6.title: 4. Advertising and marketing (optional)
section_6.description1: With your consent, we use advertising technologies from platforms such as Meta (Facebook and Instagram) and TikTok. These use pixels/tags to measure whether our ads led to enquiries, to avoid showing you ads for something you've already done, and to help us reach people who may benefit from our guidance. This may involve those platforms receiving information about your visit and setting their own cookies, acting as separate controllers under their own policies.
section_6.description2: If you decline advertising cookies, these pixels do not run. You can also manage ad personalisation directly with Meta and TikTok.

section_7.title: 5. Your Choices
section_7.description1: When you first visit YStudy you are asked to accept or decline optional (analytics and advertising) cookies. You can change your choice at any time using the "Cookie settings" link in the site footer, or by clearing cookies in your browser. Most browsers also let you block or delete cookies through their settings — though blocking strictly necessary cookies may stop parts of the site working.
section_7.description2: You can clear the tool/dashboard storage at any time by clearing your browser's site data, or by using any "reset" option provided within a tool.

section_8.title: 6. Cookies used (summary)
section_8.description1: Because the exact cookies depend on the analytics and advertising tools active on the live site, the production site should publish an up-to-date cookie table (name, provider, purpose, duration) generated from the live configuration. As a summary of categories:
section_8.description2: Necessary — consent record, security/session, tool & dashboard localStorage. Always active.
section_8.description3: Analytics — site usage measurement. Active only with consent.
section_8.description4: Advertising — Meta and TikTok pixels for campaign measurement and targeting. Active only with consent.

section_9.title: 7. How this links to your privacy rights
section_9.description: What we do with information collected through these technologies is explained in our Privacy Policy, and your data-protection rights are described in our Data Protection & GDPRTerms of Use page. To ask a question about cookies, contact privacy@ystudy.co.uk.

section_10.title: 8. Updating This Policy
section_10.description: We may update this Cookie Policy when our tools or providers change. The "last updated" date at the top shows when it last changed.

section_3.title: Your rights at a glance
section_3.description: YStudy (Dinnovi Ltd) is the data controller for the personal information you provide through our services. Under the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 you have the rights below. They are free to use, and using them will never mean you get a worse service from us.

section_4.title: The right to be informed
section_4.description: You can know what data we hold, why, and who we share it with. That is what our Privacy Policy and Cookie Policy are for.

section_5.title: The Right of Access
section_5.description: You can ask for a copy of the personal data we hold about you (a "subject access request"), and information about how we use it. We provide this free of charge and normally within one month.

section_6.title: The right to rectification
section_6.description: If any information we hold about you is wrong or incomplete — a misspelled name, an old phone number, an out-of-date qualification — you can ask us to correct it. You can also update much of this yourself in your YStudy account.

section_7.title: The Right to Erasure
section_7.description: You can ask us to delete your personal data ("the right to be forgotten") in certain circumstances — for example where it is no longer needed, or where you withdraw consent and there is no other basis for keeping it. Sometimes we must keep certain records to meet a legal obligation (for example accounting records), and we will explain if that applies.

section_8.title: The right to restrict processing
section_8.description: You can ask us to pause using your data in certain situations — for example while we check the accuracy of data you have challenged.

section_9.title: The right to object
section_9.description: You can object to processing based on our legitimate interests, and to direct marketing. If you object to marketing we will stop straight away. If you object to other processing we will stop unless we have compelling legitimate grounds that override your interests.

section_10.title: The right to data portability
section_10.description: Where we process data you provided by automated means on the basis of consent or a contract, you can ask to receive it in a common, machine-readable format, or have it sent to another provider where technically feasible.

section_11.title: The right to withdraw consent
section_11.description: Where we rely on your consent — for example marketing, advertising cookies, or processing sensitive information — you can withdraw it at any time. Withdrawing consent does not affect processing that already took place, and does not affect processing we carry out on a different lawful basis.

section_12.title: Automated decisions and profiling
section_12.description: Our online tools (such as the eligibility checker and finance calculator) give you indicative guidance to help you understand your options — they do not make a final decision about you. Decisions about funding are made by Student Finance England, and admissions decisions are made by universities. We do not carry out automated decision-making that produces legal or similarly significant effects about you without a lawful basis and appropriate safeguards.

section_13.title: How to Make a Request
section_13.description: Contact us at privacy@ystudy.co.uk, through our contact page, or by writing to Dinnovi Ltd at the registered office shown above. To protect your data, we may need to verify your identity before we act. We respond to requests within one month; if a request is particularly complex, we may extend this by up to two further months and will tell you if so.

section_14.title: Complaints
section_14.description: If you are unhappy with how we handle your data, please tell us first so we can put it right. You also have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO), the UK's data-protection regulator: ico.org.uk/make-a-complaint, helpline 0303 123 1113.
